turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. I have until 4:40, Hale. Who decided, and was Owen heard before you entered it?
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
You didn't answer my question. Was Owen heard before that zero went in, yes or no?
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.
"11:31 PM" the night before it was due. Half the seventeen-year-olds in this building start a file at that hour, so show me the document, and tell me who decided before anyone asked Owen.
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.
I'm writing down 11:52, 612, 11:58, 794. A paste from where, Hale, his own notes, his phone, another draft of his own? Turn the screen so I can read it myself.
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
Don't manage me. Turn the screen.
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.
A wrong quotation in a Grade 12 essay is a mistake, Hale, not a verdict. Which page is it on, and which three editions? Put the essay and that history in front of me, both of them.
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
Then why are we here, Hale? The essay and the history, on the table, or I'm walking down to the principal's office.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.

I'm writing down October 15, "cowardice," and "moral caution." Changing an argument between an outline and a final draft is what an outline is for, Hale. Is that outline here, and did anyone ask Owen why he changed his mind?
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.

A machine's guess, and Turnitin's own guide says the indicator "should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student"; I have it printed in my bag. Your own procedure 4.3 says software doesn't establish anything by itself. You've told me four things and shown me none of them, Hale, so turn the screen.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
There's no off the record in this room, and you're asking me how to do your job? Withdraw the zero, Hale, and then show me what you've got.
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.

"Nothing on his record," I'm writing that down, and I'll want it in an email with your name on it. You still haven't shown me one page, and you still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before that zero went in. Ten minutes, Hale.
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? I have a client call at 4:40, Hale. Owen.
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.

Take it to whoever you like on Monday; I'm going to the principal today. Procedure 4.2 says you contact me before any mark is entered, and Owen saw that zero on his phone in the middle of a class. Show me the pages or withdraw the zero, Hale.
So. Rewrite, or zero?
Neither, Hale. The zero comes off first, and then you can put anything else you're offering in writing.
